input.quote: 5. PERSONNEL. Each party agrees to assign one (1) existing sales or marketing employee primarily dedicated to assist in the sales and marketing promotional activity set forth in this Exhibit D.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-inducement covenant on Corio (our party, the licensee/customer). Full-text searches for "solicit", "hire", "recruit", "induce", "employ" and "employees" return no restrictive covenant, and every personnel-related provision is benign: Exhibit D Section 5 (Personnel) is a staffing-assignment commitment; Section 13.1-13.3 obliges Commerce One to give Corio access to its operations, consulting and engineering personnel; Section 13.5 concerns only confidentiality/invention-assignment agreements for Commerce One staff; and Section 14.5 is a standard independent-contractor status clause. Section 14.10 integrates only the NDA and Statement of Work, so no non-solicit is incorporated by reference. This is exactly the playbook's preferred position (no non-solicit on the Customer), so the deterministic checks for duration and a general-solicitation carve-out are inapplicable and no redline is warranted. We would only revisit if Commerce One later seeks to add a personnel covenant, in which case we would hold to the fallback (mutual, 12 months, services personnel only, general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, no no-hire).
